html:
SMTO-GWT-0010 — SMTO couldn't set up a secure link to the Gateway

GUID: d186fa70-45b1-4972-b307-a627515896cc
Slug: gateway-authentication-required
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gateway

What happened

  • Before sending work, SMTO needs a secure, verified link to the computer. Those checks didn't finish, so nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Edit on that Gateway, set Scheme to https, and select Save changes. SMTO only sends work over a secure connection it can verify.
  2. Expand the Gateway's row and select Check for updates. If an update is offered, install it once nothing is running there. An older Gateway may use a sign-in method this SMTO no longer accepts.
  3. If the Gateway connects to SMTO by itself (shown as Outbound), ask its manager to make sure it uses SMTO's secure (https) address. A Gateway that connects in without security is refused.
  4. Select Check connection, and when it shows Connected, run the task again. This task sent nothing yet, so running it again won't repeat any work.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway's row shows Connected and the task starts on that computer.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway. Don't paste passwords or security keys into tasks, commands or screenshots while fixing this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway authentication could not be established: the connection lacks verified HTTPS/WSS identity, pairing could not be completed, the request authentication version is unsupported, or an outbound session lacks verified identities.

What this means

  • The transport lacks required HTTPS/WSS identity verification, pairing could not be established, the request authentication version is unsupported, or an outbound session lacks verified identities. Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.

Why this can happen

  • The transport lacks required HTTPS/WSS identity verification, pairing could not be established, the request authentication version is unsupported, or an outbound session lacks verified identities.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect transport scheme, pinned identity, pairing response, protocol version and session authentication flags for the failing path.

How to fix it

  • Ensure the Gateway record uses https with a pinned TLS identity (tls_identity_spki_sha256), that outbound Gateways connect over wss, and that both sides use the same x-smto auth-version; update an older Gateway if the version is unsupported. Then rerun the health check so pairing completes before dispatch.
  • Pair or reconnect the intended Gateway through the supported pairing flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected secure transport and its controller and Gateway identities pass authentication before dispatch.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Use the retained operation phase and identity to determine effects; this explanation does not authorize retries or change pairing, target selection or execution ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
